## Response

<!-- RESPONSE-START -->
People tend to skip or ignore surveys for a lot of reasons, and honestly, I can relate. Most of us get so many survey links that it starts to feel like a chore. The textbook explains that long or confusing questionnaires can turn people away quickly, and i think that's true. If the survey feels like its going to take forever or the questions don't make sense, I'm probably not finishing it. Another big factor is motivation-- if I don't understand why the survey matters or how my responses will be used, it's easy to ignore it altogether. As someone who takes surveys, I know I am much more likely to respond if the survey looks clean, short, and easy to follow. I appreciate it when it says upfront how long it'll take and why my input is valuable. The chapter also mentions that giving people a reason to care-- like showing how their answers will make an impact-- or even offering a small incentive, can really improve response rates. Reminders help too; sometimes people just forget. Thinking about this from a research perspective, it's clear that non response can create serious bias.If only people with strong opinions or extra free time participate, the results won't represent everyone. That means researchers have to think carefully about how to design surveys that people will actually want to complete. Making them simple, respectful of people's time, and transparent about the purpose not only increases participation but also strengthens the quality of the data. In the end, good survey design is about building trust and connection with respondents, not just collecting answers. 
<!-- RESPONSE-END -->

## Word Count & Range Check

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
get_response_text <- function() {
  f <- knitr::current_input()
  if (is.null(f) || !file.exists(f)) return("")
  x <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  # Find the lines that EXACTLY match the start/end markers
  s <- grep("^<!-- RESPONSE-START -->$", x)
  e <- grep("^<!-- RESPONSE-END -->$", x)
  if (length(s) != 1 || length(e) != 1 || e <= s) return("")
  paste(x[(s + 1L):(e - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
}
count_words <- function(txt) {
  # Remove code blocks and inline code before counting
  txt <- gsub("```[\\s\\S]*?```", " ", txt, perl = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub("`[^`]*`", " ", txt, perl = TRUE)
  # Keep letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, and apostrophes
  txt <- gsub("[^\\p{L}\\p{N}\\s'-]", " ", txt, perl = TRUE)
  # Split by whitespace and count non-empty words
  words <- unlist(strsplit(txt, "\\s+", perl = TRUE))
  words <- words[nzchar(words)]
  length(words)
}
txt <- get_response_text()
n <- count_words(txt)
minw <- as.integer(params$word_min)
maxw <- as.integer(params$word_max)
in_range <- n >= minw && n <= maxw
cat(sprintf("**Word count:** %d  \n", n))
cat(sprintf("**Required range (%s):** %d–%d words  \n",
            toupper(params$course), minw, maxw))
cat(if (in_range) "**Status:** ✅ In range\n" else "**Status:** ❌ Out of range\n")
```
